prompt: In a triangle, the two angles not adjacent to a certain exterior angle measure $50°$ and $70°$. What is the measure, in degrees, of that exterior angle?
hint: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

hints.text: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.

explanation: The Exterior Angle Theorem: an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.
Check the long way: the third interior angle is $180 - 120 = 60°$, and its exterior partner is $180 - 60 = 120°$ ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Why the shortcut works
steps: The exterior angle is supplementary to its adjacent interior angle: exterior $= 180 - $ adjacent.
The three interior angles sum to $180$, so $180 - $ adjacent $=$ the other two added together.
The theorem is just those two facts combined — which is why you can always fall back on the long route if you forget it.
